page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64-lssd is an Arm-based virtual instance configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs running on the arm64 architecture. The system provides 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 5637 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 14 individual drives, providing high-capacity, low-latency local disk throughput. The instance configuration contains zero GPUs and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The arm64 processing units provide dedicated execution threads without hyperthreading flags, enabling consistent compute allocation per core. Bundling 5637 GB of local NVMe storage directly within the instance profile delivers localized disk bandwidth without network storage overhead, though local SSD storage is ephemeral and requires replication strategies for persistence. Combining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio with power-efficient Arm architecture yields high memory density and qualitative resource efficiency for memory-heavy and disk-intensive environments.

Given the substantial 512 GB memory footprint, 64 dedicated Arm cores, and 5637 GB of NVMe local storage, Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64-lssd is suited for I/O-intensive databases, in-memory caching tiers such as Redis, distributed big data processing nodes, and large-scale ETL pipelines that benefit from high local disk bandwidth and significant memory headroom.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64-lssd is an arm64-based virtual machine configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Designed without hardware accelerators, the system operates with zero GPUs and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The high memory ratio coupled with large-capacity local NVMe storage optimizes resource efficiency for workloads requiring substantial working memory and high-throughput disk operations without relying on network-attached block devices. Because the integrated NVMe storage is ephemeral, architectures require appropriate replication strategies for persistent state. This configuration serves memory-heavy workloads, distributed database engines, in-memory data analytics, high-throughput caching platforms, and data processing pipelines demanding significant local disk bandwidth.
